en:
You want to hear my story?
I see... Then shall I tell the second scary story?
My name is Akemi Iwashita.
I'm a third-year.
You know, before I tell this story, there's something I'd like to ask you.
{a}... that's what you said your name was, wasn't it?
Do you mind?
Even if you say you do, I'll be asking anyway.
Well then, ready?{p}Are you a kind person?
I'm kind
I'm not kind
I can't say either way

Heh heh heh... Quite something, to say that about yourself.
Either you're terribly sure of yourself, or you really are kind.
Well, never mind.
One look in your eyes will tell me which it is.{p}
Are you someone who can keep any promise, whatever it is?
I can keep my promises
I can't keep my promises
It depends on the situation

I see.
What a wonderful person you are.
Everyone must be very fond of you.
Someone like you is rare. A precious thing.
This is the first time I've ever met anyone like that.
Well then, let me ask you one more question.
...{a}.{p}

Are you the type who can take other people's advice to heart?
Even when your own opinion is different from theirs.{p}Well?
I can take it to heart
I can't do that
Depends on who's giving it

Heh heh... I just knew you'd answer that way.
You truly are the perfect human being.
I'm so happy to have met someone like you.
I hope we'll know each other for a long time to come.
Heh heh heh heh...{p}

This is the story of a tragedy that one boy happened to stumble into.
That day, he had been kept late for a make-up class.
Let's see, his name was... yes, for now, let's call him this.
{b} {a}.
It's a nice name, isn't it?
I'm sorry.
I don't know that boy's name either, you see.
So I'll borrow your name for him.
{b} {a}.
...It's a lovely name, truly.{p}

The make-up class went like this: they were handed a worksheet, and whoever solved the problems on it could go home.
There were quite a few hard problems on it.
They weren't the kind you could solve easily.
And they were the sort of students who end up in make-up classes in the first place, you know.
Not exactly the type who love to study.
So they scribbled down any old answers and went to show them to the teacher.
Then they got the teacher's go-ahead and hurried off home.
I suppose the teacher understood how it was, too.
Well, it was a make-up class in name only.
But he was different.
He sat down to the worksheet in earnest.
He wasn't the kind of person who breaks a promise.
Even if it's only a promise to a teacher, once you've made it, you have to keep it, don't you?
Just like you, really.
So he stayed behind alone in the classroom, trying to solve it to the very end.
Problems he couldn't find so much as a hint for, however hard he thought.
"What, you're still here?
I forgot all about you. You can go home now, {a}."
The teacher had been sure everyone had already gone home.
The classroom light was on, so the teacher looked in, suspicious, and found one student still there.
Awful, isn't it?
Well, since the teacher had given permission, he got ready to go home, and when he happened to look around, it had already gone completely dark.{p}

Everything around him had gone dead quiet.
No one was there.{p}

He had been left all alone in the dark school.
The only light came from dim fluorescent lamps, glowing so weakly they seemed about to go out.
There was only the dry clack, clack, clack of his footsteps echoing; no other sound could be heard.
The students who played in the schoolyard after class, the students who worked up a sweat at their clubs... none of them were left.
He glanced at the clock: eight thirty.
It had gotten so late that even he was surprised.
His classroom was on the third floor of the new school building.{p}

In front of him were stairs leading down to the second floor, and at the far end of the hallway stretching straight ahead was another staircase down to the second floor.
Whichever way he chose, the distance to the school gate wasn't much different.{p}Which one would you choose?
Take the stairs right in front
Take the stairs at the end of the straight hallway

I see, so that's the way you choose.
Heh heh heh... He did the same.
He decided to go through the long hallway and down the stairs at the far end.
That was the way he always went home.{p}

A long, straight hallway is truly frightening to walk at night.
The lights are few and far between, so your feet slow down on their own.
Even when you think you're hurrying, walking fast, somehow you end up slower.
"That's weird."
He muttered it under his breath.
For some reason, the hallway felt longer than usual.
Normally he'd have reached the end long ago and be heading down the stairs by now.
And yet the hallway just went on and on.
He walked and walked, and though he could see the stairs ahead, they never got any closer.
Thinking this was strange, he looked back...{p}

There was proof, all right, of how far he had walked.
He really had covered as much of the hallway as he thought he had.{p}

Thinking it was odd, he faced forward again, and a long hallway still stretched out ahead of him.
"Was this hallway always this long?"
He tilted his head, puzzled.
It was his first time walking through the school at night, so maybe he just couldn't judge the distance.
He tried telling himself that, too.
But even so, something about it gave him the creeps.{p}
What will you do?{p}Will you keep going down the hallway?
Keep going down the hallway
Turn back to the starting point

"This is definitely weird."
Muttering to himself, he decided to turn back.
Somehow he sensed it would be dangerous to keep going.
But once he turned back, he couldn't get back to where he'd been, no matter how long he walked.
He was sure he had walked farther than before, and yet he never managed to reach the place he started from.
"What on earth is going on?"
He turned around once more.{p}

The hallway still stretched on and on.
Ahead of him and behind him, the long hallway ran on for exactly the same distance.
It felt as if the fluorescent lights had grown dimmer than before.
The light was so weak now that he couldn't see the end of the hallway.
Beyond the gloom, he could only vaguely sense the stairs.
And even that was a faint, uncertain sense.{p}

"Aaaaaaaagh!"
He screamed at the top of his lungs to drown out his fear, and ran.
He ran like a madman.
Forgetting all about the rule against running in the halls.{p}

"Ow!"
Maybe he'd strained too hard, because his own momentum sent him sprawling.
"Owww..."
Luckily, he wasn't hurt.
He'd only banged his elbows and knees hard, and he managed to stand.{p}

He got up and looked around once more... It didn't feel as if he'd gotten any farther at all.
However he looked at it, he was still right around the middle of the long hallway.
To be precise, both ends were wrapped in darkness by now, so he couldn't see them clearly.
He strained his eyes and took a good, hard look down the long hallway once more.
Even so, the dim hallway would never show him what lay beyond, in the darkness.
But as he strained his eyes, he froze in shock.{p}

What will you do?
Will you run?{p}Or else...
Go closer
Run away

It was creepy enough as it was. There was no way he could go near something so incomprehensible.
{a} ran.
Fighting the feeling that his legs would give out, he ran for his life.
But no matter how far forward he went, the hallway wouldn't end.
He ran until he was out of breath, ran and ran and ran with everything he had, until at last he collapsed where he was.
It was agony; he felt like he would choke.
He coughed so violently that with every breath it felt as if his heart would come up along with it.
Even so, his position hadn't changed.
It was like running the wrong way on a conveyor belt.{p}

Suddenly, there was a sound behind him.
The rustle of something moving.{p}

He felt sweat break out all over his body.
...What's wrong?
Isn't that sweat on your face?
This isn't about you, you know.
This is the story of the other {a}.{p}Will you turn around?
Turn around
Don't turn around

And then, what do you think happened?
Up ahead, he could see that black shadow from before!
He'd run away from that black lump, yet somehow it was in front of him.
Thinking it was strange, he slowly looked back.{p}

And then... it was behind him too.
That black, squirming, wriggling thing.{p}

He couldn't stop his body from shaking and trembling.
After all, there was no escape now.
Hell if he went forward, hell if he went back.
Whichever way he went, he couldn't escape that black lump.{p}What will you do?
Go forward
Go back
Huddle down right there

He gathered his courage and set off, one step at a time.
More than courage, maybe it was closer to resignation.
He still couldn't see the end of the hallway, but he could tell the black thing was gradually getting closer.
In time with his slow steps, the thing began to take on a clear shape.{p}

It was a girl.
A girl in a school uniform was sitting there, huddled against the wall.
All at once, his fear was blown away.
He let out a sigh of relief and ran over to her.
What feels frightening alone feels reassuring when there are two of you.{p}

...She was crying.
She had her face covered, and all he could hear was her sobbing.
"What's wrong?
Did something happen to you here?"
He called out to her.
Through the gaps between the hands covering her face, she peered up at him with two bulging eyes.
"...My leg... my leg hurts so much I can't walk.
...So I'm resting.
...Please... help me."
She murmured it in a tiny, broken voice.
She had gently drawn her legs up, as if to protect the one that hurt.{p}

Don't you think it's strange for a girl to be in a place like this, all by herself?
You do, don't you?
What will you do?
Will you help her?{p}Or will you leave her be?
Help her
Leave her there and run away

What?
What did you just say?{p}Say that once more for me.
Help her
Leave her there and run away

I hope I didn't hear you wrong...
Did you just say you'd run away and leave an injured girl all alone?
That's what you said, isn't it?
You just told me yourself that you were kind.
Am I wrong?
Or have my ears gone funny?
I'm sure I heard you say it.
You're kind, aren't you.
So go on, help her.
I absolutely hate being lied to.
When someone lies to me, it makes me want to kill them.
Understand?
If you lie again, I'll kill you.
Don't you dare lie.{p}

You're kind, after all.
So you will help her.{p}

"Are you okay?
I'll carry you on my back."
You gently helped her up and carried her on your back.
And she said:
"...Thank you.
...Don't let go of me."
You're kind, after all.{p}You know how you answered her, don't you?
Sure
No way

Right.
That's what you answered.
Because you're a kind person.
Of course you did.
And then you slowly began to walk.{p}

Her body was cold, but she was very light.
So light it felt as though you weren't carrying anyone at all.
Even so, you could feel her thin hands winding around your neck.
Not being alone gave you just a little courage.
But the end of the hallway wasn't getting any closer.{p}
It didn't feel like you were moving forward at all.{p}

What's more, you began to hear a strange noise behind you.
Come to think of it, there had been a black lump at the other end of the hallway too, hadn't there?
In the end, you never found out what it was.
Maybe that was what was making the noise.
Should you turn around, or not... you couldn't decide.{p}
Just then, her breath brushed against your ear.{p}

"...Don't turn around.
You mustn't turn around.
If you turn around, something terrible will happen...
Whatever you do, you mustn't turn around."
Unlike her cold body, her breath was lukewarm.
A nasty breath that tickled your ear.
As if to escape that breath, you dropped your gaze.
And then your eyes fell on her hands.{p}

You were so startled you nearly threw her off.
Her hands were dry and withered, just like a mummy's.
Thin hands, with a single layer of skin clinging to the bone almost apologetically.
The fingers seemed to be nothing but bone.{p}

"What's wrong?
You're shaking.
Are you cold?
If you're cold, I'll warm you up."
The voice whispering in your ear was very gentle.
Even so, it also seemed hoarse somehow, like the voice of a withered old woman.
Now and then her hair brushed your cheek, and it was pure white.
When you'd helped her up, it should have been long black hair, sleek and damp, yet what you saw now was white hair that stood out starkly against the darkness.{p}

Who on earth was it you were carrying on your back?
Maybe it wasn't even human.
If you turned around, you'd know the answer.
What will you do?{p}Will you turn around?
Turn around
Don't turn around

Right.
You're someone who listens to advice, aren't you?
Yes, you have to listen to her advice.
You must not look back.
No matter what happens.
You told me so yourself, after all.
That you listen to advice.
Don't lie to me.
If you lie, I'll kill you.
I hate it.
I can't forgive liars.
Understood?
...You didn't look back.
Even so, the fear didn't go away.
With every step you took, the fear soaked deeper into every inch of you.{p}

And then the girl's hands, wrapped around your neck, began to feel as if they were squeezing.
Somehow, it was very hard to breathe.
With each jolt of your steps, her hands were without a doubt tightening around your neck.
Thin, cold, hard fingers were coiled firmly around your throat.
If you looked back, she might vanish.
If you shook her off, you might get away from her.{p}What will you do?
Turn around
Shake her off
Do nothing

My, how admirable of you.
If you turned around, you'd be ignoring her advice.
If you shook her off, you'd be breaking your promise to her.
You endured it desperately.
Yes, shielding a heart that felt ready to freeze solid with fear, you endured.{p}

"...This hallway is so long, isn't it?
...I wonder when this hallway will ever end.
Was there ever a hallway this long at school...?"
Her voice, spoken to no one in particular, melted away into the darkness.
"...It's awfully cold, isn't it?"{p}

The moment she said that, a cold wind blew at you from behind.
And riding on the wind came a groaning voice, as if wrung from the pit of someone's belly.
A dank, hateful voice, like the dead of hell cursing and reviling the living from the depths of the earth.
It might have been the sound of the wind.
But then again, it might not have been the wind at all.
Her voice whispered at your ear again.
"...Scared, aren't ya?
Wanna try looking back?
Look back, and you can rest easy. You won't have to be scared anymore."{p}

A sweet, beckoning voice.
What will you do?
Will you look back?{p}If you don't look back, you might die.
Look back
Don't look back

"Eeeeeeeeeek!"
Suddenly an ear-splitting, high-pitched shriek rang out, and the thin fingers wrapped around your neck clenched tight.
"Stop it!"
That was all you could manage to scream.
...And then, you slipped away into unconsciousness.{p}

......I'm sorry.
It wasn't you, was it?
It was the other {a}.
Yes, this was the story of the other you.
It was the next morning when he came to.
A student from his class helped him up.{p}

"What happened to you?
Why are you sleeping in a place like this?"
Even when asked that, he didn't know how to answer.
As his head cleared, he hurriedly looked up and down the hallway.{p}

The hallway was plainly visible in the morning light.
The usual hallway was there.
The usual hallway, where you could see from one end to the other.
And he had been lying in front of his classroom.
"...I made it."
That was all he could murmur.
Maybe it had been a dream.
Maybe he'd been worn out from studying and had a bad dream.
The classmate was giving him a strange look.
And then the classmate said:
"What's with you?
You've got a weird bruise on your neck."
At that, he checked in a mirror.{p}

On his neck were distinct finger marks, as if he had been strangled.
In the end, he never found out why the hallway had been so long.
Or what it was he had been carrying on his back.
If he had looked behind him, he might have learned what it really was.
Though he might have lost his life in exchange.{p}

The bruise on his neck didn't fade for about a month.
Even so, he survived.
Maybe it was thanks to keeping his promise to the very end.
You said you were in Class 1-E, didn't you?
If I remember right, that classroom is on the third floor.
Isn't Class 1-E that classroom at the end of the long hallway?{p}

But don't worry.
You're a kind person who keeps promises and listens to advice.
I'll pray that never changes.
Humans are creatures who change their minds so easily, after all.
...Heh heh heh heh, do be careful.
And that's the end of my story.
Now, who's speaking next?{p}

What a thing to say, out of nowhere.
Don't say such sad things.
Then I'm asking you, please.
Become a kind person from now on.
Otherwise, I can't talk with you.
I like kind people.
Now, give me your answer.{p}Are you a kind person?
I'm kind
I'm not kind

You're not confident in your own kindness?
It's all right.
I can tell.
You're a kind person.
Aren't you?
I want you to be able to say that you are.
I like kind people, you see.
Now, give me your answer.{p}Are you a kind person?
I'm kind
I'm not kind

I see...
So that's the kind of person you are.
Fine. Then promise me.
Promise that from now on, you'll be someone who keeps promises.
Please.
Now, I'll ask you once more.{p}Are you someone who can keep a promise?
I can keep my promises
I can't keep my promises

Don't put it like that.
Whenever you make a promise to someone, be the kind of person who always keeps it.
Please.
If you agree, give me your answer.
{a}...{p}You can keep a promise, can't you?
I can keep my promises
I can't keep my promises

Thank you.
You're a good person, aren't you?{p}
Then I'll ask you my last question.{p}

Heh heh...
Because this school is far too dangerous.
A tremendous spiritual aura swirls all through it.
Meeting you here, right now, must be some kind of fate.{p}

Listen, {a}.
Make sure you listen to other people's advice.
Otherwise...
I won't answer for whatever happens to you.
Now, give me your answer.{p}Do you listen to other people's advice?
I take people's advice to heart
I can't do that

I see...
That's one way to think, too.
But that won't get you anywhere at this school.
If you don't listen to all sorts of people's advice, you'll regret it later.
This school is far too dangerous.
A tremendous spiritual aura swirls all through it.
Meeting you here, right now, must be some kind of fate.
Listen, {a}.
Make sure you listen to other people's advice.
Otherwise...
I won't answer for whatever happens to you.
Now, give me your answer once more.{p}Do you listen to other people's advice?
I take people's advice to heart
I can't do that

I see...
What a shame.
I thought that if you were a kind person, you might be able to break the curse of the girl I'm about to tell you about...
This is the story of a pitiful girl.
I don't know how you'll feel about it, but that's how I see her.
This is the story of a pitiful girl.{p}

Long ago, there was a girl at this school named Natsumi Kitajima.
There was a boy she liked.
His name was... what was it, now?
I can't remember.
Let's see, suppose we call him {a}.
I'll borrow your name.
His name was {b} {a}.{p}

Kitajima just couldn't bring herself to confess.
She was in the same class as {a}, but day after day went by with her doing nothing but gazing at him from afar.{p}

And then, one hot summer day...
She was gazing at {a}, the way she always did.{p}

{a}'s face, {a}'s hair, {a}'s arms peeking out of his shirt...
She had extremely sharp eyes; they say she could even see the beads of sweat running down his arm.
And then a mosquito landed there.
He slapped the mosquito with his hand.
And a tiny smear of blood was left on {a}'s arm.
When she saw it, she felt a little strange.{p}

Outside the window, the cicadas were shrilling almost deafeningly.
A hot, hot summer day...
Looking at the mosquito that had sucked {a}'s blood, she found herself feeling somehow envious.
That mosquito could land on {a}'s arm and even drink his blood, and she envied it terribly.
She was so far away from him, and yet that mosquito...{p}

Day after day, mosquito after mosquito landed on his arm.
It made her feel awful.
She couldn't even speak to {a}, and yet those mosquitoes...
She brooded over it until she even came to think that if she could drink {a}'s blood, she wouldn't mind being swatted dead like a mosquito.
Kitajima was terrified of herself for feeling that way.
So she decided to confess to {a}.
She gathered every ounce of courage and decided to tell him how she felt.{p}...How will you answer her?
Go out with her
Turn her down

The next day, the two of you decided to eat lunch together on the roof.
A boxed lunch, eaten together with her...
She looked so happy.
A happy time went on for a while.
But...{p}

While you were eating your rolled omelet, she suddenly slapped your arm.
"I'm sorry.
There was a mosquito just now..."
That's what Kitajima said.{p}After that, she began slapping your arms and face at every chance she got.
Keep going out with her
Get away from her

And her behavior escalated more and more.
She simply could not forgive the mosquitoes for sucking your blood.
{a} is mine.
And yet the mosquitoes are still sucking {a}'s blood...
Whenever she thought about it, she was beside herself.
She couldn't forgive the mosquitoes that drank your blood, but she also grew unable to forgive you, for letting them drink it so easily.
And she became even more violent toward you than before.
When you scolded her for it, she burst into tears.{p}

After that, she couldn't stop thinking about your windpipe.
Every time you talked, she couldn't stop thinking about the way the flesh of your throat moved.
I might as well just...
She thought that, over and over again.
And then, one day...{p}

As you were eating lunch on the roof as usual, she suddenly sank her teeth into your windpipe...
It seems she was ready to die right then and there.
If she could drink your blood, she didn't care if she died.
That's how determined she was.
She bit into you with all her might.{p}

So hard that your throat could have torn right off...
...
You fought back desperately and pinned her down.
Word of it spread around the school, and she transferred away.
And then...{p}

From then on, swarms of mosquitoes began breeding in the class she had been in.
And their target was... {a}, it was you.
No, it wasn't you, was it?
It was the {a} in this story.
The mosquitoes in that class didn't drink the blood of any other student.
They say they drank only {a}'s blood, every day, day after day.
They say that every day, day after day, they fed on his flesh all over his body...
A rumor went around the school that it was Kitajima's curse.
And they say that curse still hangs over that class today.{p}

That class was... Class 1-E.
Your class.
The curse, it seems, is that something speaks into the ear of a girl with an unrequited crush.
They say the voice says this:
"Make the one you love yours and yours alone.
To do that, you must drink their blood.
If you can't do it, I'll do it for you.
Well? Shall I send the mosquitoes under my command to drink their blood for you?"
And depending on how the girl answers, mosquitoes swarm through the class.{p}

...I feel sorry for Kitajima.
I'm sure she was led astray by whoever owns that voice.
I don't think the mosquito swarms were her curse.
It must have been something in this school...
that led her astray, I believe.
{a}.
If a girl who fell for you heard that voice, what would you do?
I wonder if you could break the curse of that voice's owner...
That's the end of my story.
Whose turn is it next?{p}

Why would you have to turn her down?
She was so very sweet and modest.
So {a} was overjoyed when she confessed to him.
And he decided to go out with her.
Listen.
You knew nothing of the terrible feelings that had taken root in her heart.{p}

You started to think there was something strange about the way she acted.
So one day, after some time had passed, you brought up breaking up with her.{p}

Then she burst into tears and clung to your chest.
She thought:
And just when I thought I'd finally gotten close enough to talk to him.
If I break up with {a}, the days of watching him from afar will start all over again.
I can't bear that...
As she was thinking that, her eyes fell on your throat.{p}

She remembered the mosquitoes that drank your blood, and an aching feeling came over her.
And then she did something even she could hardly believe.{p}

Yes, she sank her teeth into your windpipe.
She bit down with all her might.{p}

You'd say a thing like that?
That's a problem. There was something I wanted you to promise me...
I have a favor to ask of you, since you're so kind.
I want you to break the curse I'm about to tell you about.
...It may be an impossible thing to ask.
But I can't help telling you about it.
Because I feel so very sorry for the girl in this story.
...Listen carefully.{p}

I see...
I had a favor to ask of you, kind as you are...
There was something I wanted you to promise me.
I wanted you to break the curse I'm about to tell you about.
But you're someone who can't take other people's advice, aren't you?{p}

Then perhaps it's hopeless.
I doubt you could ever take advice from me.
Still, I'll tell you.
About an incident that happened at this school long ago.
Your class is in danger.
...Consider yourself warned.
Well then, let's begin the story.{p}

I see, so that's the way you choose.
The same as him.
Perhaps the two of you think alike.
He went down the stairs right in front of him.
He went down from the third floor to the floor below, and when he happened to look down the hallway...{p}

There was his own classroom.
He was sure he had gone down the stairs.
But this was the third floor, no doubt about it.
What will you do?{p}Will you try going down the stairs again?
Go down the stairs again
Go along the hallway ahead

"I'll try it one more time."
He went down the stairs again.
He was getting frantic, and without meaning to he quickened his pace.
He nearly tripped...{p}
He clung to the wall.{p}

There was his own classroom.
Even though he was sure he had gone down the stairs.
No matter how many times he went down, he always arrived on the third floor.
He gave up on these stairs and decided to walk down the hallway in front of him.
He would go home by the stairs at the far end.{p}

He decided to just keep going.
Considering how far he had already walked, going forward should get him home sooner than turning back.
Stifling the bad feeling spreading deep in his chest, he kept walking.
......He heard something.
Startled, he froze in his tracks.{p}

He convinced himself of that and started walking again.
Then he heard it again.
And it wasn't just one voice.
Stifled giggles were coming from all over the dark hallway.
This was no trick of his ears.
He knew it for certain.
Someone was here.
He strained his eyes, but there was no one there.
And yet the voices kept coming.{p}

Then suddenly, as if the darkness itself had congealed, a black shadow appeared in front of him.
He stopped.
......At some point, the laughter had stopped.
But he was so absorbed by the shadow before him that he didn't even notice.{p}

The black shadow was squirming by the wall.
It looked like a lump of flesh, or a garbage bag.
But those movements clearly belonged to a living creature with a will of its own.
Then what on earth could it be?{p}

He gathered his courage and slowly started walking.
Carefully, softly, softly, he crept closer to the black shadow.{p}

Peering through the gloom, he could tell it was a person.
A girl, in fact, wearing a sailor uniform.
She was crouched down, trembling.
Maybe she was crying.
He worked up his nerve and was about to call out to her.{p}

At that very moment.
She turned around, and when he saw her, he was so shocked his breath stopped.{p}

Huge, glinting, goggling eyes, and below them a tiny, shriveled chin and cracked lips.
